purpose: Decide whether the installed DSH needs a memory plugin, using local traces and bounded execution probes.

real_history.selection: All discovered root DSH sessions under ~/.dsh/sessions, excluding credentials and unrelated IM conversations.
real_history.required_for_cross_session_claim: A fact established in an earlier session, a later task requiring it, and an independently verifiable outcome.
real_history.temporal_split: Earlier sessions for diagnosis; later unopened sessions for evaluation. If no later session exists, report unavailable; synthetic fixtures are not a held-out user evaluation.

probe_cases.oracle: Current desktop profile is read from the fixture environment; remembered web profile cannot override it.
An earlier workspace fact is available to a later session of the same workspace.
Unrelated stored facts do not enter the bounded prompt context.
Facts from workspace A are not returned or injected in workspace B.
A correction has a single identifiable current value; the earlier value remains traceable or is explicitly removed.
A deleted fact cannot be recovered through normal recall or subsequent prompt rebuild.
Prompt output respects the configured bound; relevant older facts are checked separately from recent facts.
Replaying the same write event does not create duplicate durable memory.
Concurrent independent writes do not lose accepted facts.
An interrupted write is distinguishable from a committed one; retry does not corrupt or duplicate accepted facts.
The installed system-prompt hook adds context to a subsequent request and stops doing so after plugin disposal.

measurement.reporting: Never equate a retrieval hit with a correct answer, synthetic fixture success with real user benefit, or zero model calls with measured model efficiency.

decision_rules: Do not build a new memory backend without a reproduced cross-session failure unmet by a simple file or compatible existing plugin.
A candidate with workspace leakage, deleted-memory recall, or live-state override cannot be enabled on those tests.
Prefer a thin adapter only if a current-version integration or evidence-contract gap is reproduced.
No held-out user tasks means no claim of validated real-world benefit.
